A friend once told me approvingly that someone she knew had talked his schizophrenic adult son into having a vasectomy. Though I read “talked into” as “coerced,” I didn’t say anything.
Oh my god, I thought instead, maybe I shouldn’t be a mother. I’d had a break with reality after stopping my antipsychotic 10 years before, frustrated with weight gain. I had returned to taking medication and my mental health had stabilized long before this conversation. But I was now pursuing pregnancy.
Despite my master’s and a writing career that included Psychology Today essays, my successful marriage, and a 10-year history of treatment adherence and stability, I wondered if I would be too unstable to parent. I’d overdosed multiple times while psychotic, including twice within two weeks. In one incident, I ran away from the group home where I had been institutionalized, eating Benadryl tablets like M&Ms and knocking them back with Budweiser, then drove in a blackout. The last thing I remember —
My hands on the steering wheel as I accelerated up a freeway on ramp.
While psychotic, I’d been a danger both to myself and others. Would I become a danger to a child?
The maternal mental health needs of women like me have been badly under-prioritized in American society. It takes a tragic case like Lindsay Clancy’s for people to realize reproductive psychiatry is even a medical field, much less recognize its critical importance. When she started spiraling into postpartum psychosis, Clancy’s husband, Patrick, didn’t understand the danger, as he said Sunday night in a “60 Minutes” interview: “I could piece together what it was like to be really, really anxious or depressed. But I didn’t know how to manage a postpartum illness.”
Many women with a history of mental illness get pregnant; others who were previously healthy experience symptoms for the first time while pregnant. Thirteen percent of all pregnant women use selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor antidepressants (SSRIs), according to Maria Muzik, a psychiatry and obstetrics and gynecology professor at the University of Michigan and the director of its Perinatal and Reproductive Psychiatry Clinic. Eighty percent of them obtain their prescription from an OB-GYN rather than a psychiatrist, she told me. And, though the experience of severe mental illness and motherhood remain almost invisible in popular discussion, more than 100,000 women with severe mental illnesses have children every year in the United States. Most women with serious mental health conditions like schizophrenia and bipolar disorder are mothers.
These women often experience gaps in care like Clancy’s. Average inpatient psychiatric hospitalization stays are five to seven days. Many outpatient psychiatrists and therapists don’t take insurance. When they do, copays can be a significant barrier. Vast areas of the country, particularly rural regions, are deserts for psychiatric care and reproductive psychiatric care. Muzik estimated there might currently be six to 10 practicing reproductive psychiatrists in the entire state of Michigan. Only 6% to 8% of women with peripartum depression receive adequate psychiatric treatment, and suicide and homicide combined are the leading cause of maternal mortality in the United States.
After deciding to start a family, my husband and I sought prenatal counseling on the safety of my medication regimen in pregnancy and my potential for relapse at a university medical center. But this potentially lifesaving prenatal care remains out of reach for many women with serious mental illness, 20% of whom are uninsured.
To fill the gap in reproductive psychiatric treatment, practitioners are developing a workaround — maternal mental health consultation hotlines like UMass Chan Medical School’s Lifeline for Moms or the University of Michigan’s MC3, with a phone line Muzik staffs every Friday. These hotlines are a critically important innovation, allowing primary care physicians, nurse practitioners, and OB-GYNs to receive real-time guidance from specialists, improving clinician confidence.
But they have become a substitute for the specialized workforce the country has never built. Imagine asking primary care physicians to manage leukemia over the phone because oncologists were so scarce — we’d recognize there was a problem.
Even more damagingly, women often receive care from practitioners who declare they are specialists but have no real reproductive psychiatry training, according to Lauren Osborne, the vice chair of clinical research in the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology at Weill Cornell Medicine. “Anybody can hang out a shingle and say, ‘I’m a reproductive psychiatrist,’ and there’s nothing to say that somebody is or is not,” she said. “People who have more severe versions of these [mental health] disorders, who are seeking out help and expertise, find somebody they think is qualified, and that person isn’t, and things get missed, and there can be tragic consequences.”
Training in reproductive psychiatry is inconsistent, with expertise remaining concentrated at universities. Despite the complexity of treating psychiatric illness during pregnancy and the severe need, the United States still has no formal reproductive psychiatry subspecialty or standardized national training pathway. The American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology requires that a general psychiatry subspecialty reach a certain number of fellowships and trainees in those fellowships to be formally approved, Osborne told me. At least 25 fellowships with 50 trainees enrolled are needed; 18 programs, nearly all of which have a single trainee and all of which differ, currently exist in reproductive psychiatry.
“It’s probably 15 or 20 years, even as quickly as the specialty is growing, before we could reach that [threshold], and maybe even longer because there’s no money to support these fellowships,” Osborne said.
If they become pregnant, women who experience psychosis often have little support. And psychosis is a uniquely traumatizing condition. My husband and I sometimes laugh about my delusions: how, during my psychotic break, I believed a fellow psychiatric patient with religious delusions was a Vatican assassin, hunting me down, her repetition of the word “tray” code for “prey.” How I thought my grandmother plotted to kill my cats, so I packed them in their carriers, put them in the backseat, and attempted to cross the Blue Water Bridge from Michigan into Ontario without a passport.
These stories are funny — and not. People experiencing such devastating delusions deserve humane, quality care. With such care, we are capable of leading rich, fulfilling lives —
And even being good parents.
A solution is taking shape to the maternal mental health care crisis. Realizing they can’t wait 20 years or longer, Muzik, Osborne, and other leading clinicians and advocates have founded a nonprofit organization that is working to establish its own board certification exam. Many other specialties, including obesity and breastfeeding medicine, have followed a similar path to certification, Osborne told me.
This nonprofit, the North American Board of Reproductive Psychiatry, is beginning to establish a set of standards. For instance, to be eligible to sit for the exam, a clinician will have had to complete a fellowship in reproductive psychiatry or consult-liaison psychiatry, or have substantial clinical practice and some continuing medical education, according to Osborne.
“We’re hoping eventually that money earned from that exam can then be fed back in to form more fellowships,” she said. “We would eventually love to see this be something where, to be a qualified reproductive psychiatrist to sit for that exam, you have to have done [a] fellowship, but we need a pathway to increase the numbers of fellowships. Our approach was to tackle the board certification first and use that as a path to then create more fellowships.”
Osborne also directs the National Curriculum in Reproductive Psychiatry, what amounts to a fellowship-length education for reproductive psychiatry. Osborne estimates that most of the fellows from the currently established reproductive psychiatry fellowships are now training in it, along with many fellows from the related consult-liaison specialty, an important step to regulating this care in the United States.
The North American Board of Reproductive Psychiatry is actively fundraising to mount the first exam and publicizing its work.
The reproductive needs of women with serious mental illness deserve to be considered, our right to make decisions for ourselves honored. Clinicians should be working to support us, not fumbling incompetently or making paternalistic determinations. With proper support, we can make informed reproductive choices.
My husband and I pursued parenthood for several years before choosing not to have children: We both had serious reservations about my ability to handle intense stress and insomnia.
However, I recently sustained what might have been a miscarriage: I was showing telltale signs of an accidental pregnancy, too early for a test. It was my mom who said to me, in the depths of my grief: “Meggie, you’re allowed to choose your health.”
I remember walking in the bright spring sunlight up and down the street from our little blue house — up and down, up and down — and thinking, My god, I can choose to be well.
And that’s, in the end, what I did.
Quality maternal mental health care promotes reproductive agency. But consultation hotlines are all too often the only option of providing it. Clinician volunteerism and workarounds are not the answer to the critical need for specialty treatment.
Instead, reproductive psychiatry must be treated as a workforce worthy of major investment. Without a significant commitment of resources, pregnant patients with mental health issues will continue to depend on extraordinarily dedicated individual doctors, rather than affordable, accessible care, and tragedies like that of Clancy and her family will continue to happen.
Women like me don’t need to be protected from motherhood. We need a health care system that will enable us to make our own informed decisions about it.
An MFA in writing and a Psychology Today and HuffPost contributor, Meg LeDuc writes about maternal mental health on her Substack, the Mother Prescription, and is working on a memoir.

Quick Answer
The ASUS ProArt PZ14 is a powerful 2-in-1 Windows tablet for creators, with a sharp 3K OLED display, strong Snapdragon X2 Elite performance, excellent battery life, and full desktop apps. However, its high price, weak touch experience, and some ARM app limits hold it back.
People still debate why the tablet category exists. Some people believe they can replace laptops, while others see them as glorified smartphones with bigger screens.
I agree with both statements, as tablets are extremely portable. They are thinner, lighter, and easy to carry anywhere, and they can also convert into a laptop on the go, with the added advantage of a stylus for note-taking, sketching, or even marking up PDF files. Not to mention, they’re also great for watching movies and other entertainment.
But they are extremely limited in software capabilities despite hardware that can run fully native desktop applications. But Apple’s software limitations are also a deal-breaker for many. On the other hand, it runs the full Windows 11 OS on tablets without limitations. But it isn’t optimized for tablets.
For most people, or for creative work, the iPad is the first choice. But I recently got a chance to review the ASUS ProArt PZ14, which is a 2-in-1, tablet-first Windows device designed for creative work that is portable and offers an excellent OLED screen, solid performance, solid battery life, and is capable of running fully native applications, and comes with a keyboard and a pen out of the box for all your creative work and note-taking. I have been using the ASUS ProArt PZ14 for the past two weeks. In this detailed review, you will find out whether the ASUS ProArt PZ14 breaks tradition by doing things differently. Or is it just another tablet in the debate? Let’s find out.
Table of Contents
ASUS ProArt PZ14 Design and Build: Lightweight and practical, but the design is an acquired taste
ASUS ProArt PZ14 is a tablet-first Windows PC. The keyboard detaches completely from the tablet, and all components, including the processor, sit on the back of the display.
As a result, it carries all the weight. ASUS includes a magnetic case in the box that you can attach to the back of the tablet to use as a stand and to hold the ASUS Pen 3.0. I wouldn’t recommend attaching it without the case because, while you’re holding the tablet, the magnets are not strong, and it can easily fall off, which it did. But hopefully, thanks to the build, it survived accidental falls.
Thanks to the matte finish, the back of the tablet isn’t a fingerprint magnet either, but stains are visible if you look at it a certain way, and they wipe off easily with any standard cloth.
An ASUS design choice on the back can be a hit or a miss depending on your perception. Right off the bat, the ASUS ProArt PZ14 doesn’t look like a tablet. It felt like a very niche tablet designed for a specific purpose. It has a single rear camera. Thankfully, there is no bump, and it comes with a lot of stickers, which indicates it is more than just a tablet.
You get ProArt branding at the top in the center. Overall, the fit and finish are solid, but the looks can be hit or miss based on your perception. I wish it looked more like a tablet.
The ASUS ProArt PZ14 comes with dual speakers, with one on each side The power button is on the top in landscape and on the right in portrait, which is convenient for landscape use but less convenient in portrait.
And you can find the volume-down and volume-up keys on the right as well, making it easy to control with your right hand. The SD Express 7.0 card reader and two USB4 Type-C ports are on the left side.
The look changes entirely from the front. It comes with a 14-inch 3K OLED display with a 144Hz refresh rate and minimal bezels, similar to the iPad Pro, but wider overall. At the top, you get an 8MP IR front camera with no privacy shutter.
The tablet weighs just 790 grams, making it lightweight and easy to use, but the larger display is hard to hold for long periods when using it as a tablet. The tablet has rounded corners on the back, which make it easy to hold for long periods, and the textured finish on the front half provides better grip. The matte finish makes it less slippery.
The ASUS ProArt PZ14 also has an IP52 rating. ASUS officially claims that it is tested to MIL-STD-810Hstandards . So you have the military standard, but don’t drop-test it like other laptops.
When I first held the ASUS ProArt PZ14, the back finish felt like plastic. However, ASUS claims the chassis uses an aluminum alloy. The sides feel very solid.
ASUS ProArt PZ14 Display: A gorgeous 3K OLED made for creators
The ASUS ProArt PZ14 display is one of the best-looking, and if there is one reason to choose this tablet, it’s this display. Whether you are a business user, a graphic designer, or someone who wants to casually watch movies and play games, it delivers a great viewing experience.
The ASUS ProArt PZ14 comes with a 14-inch 3K OLED display. It comes with a 144Hz refresh rate for a smooth experience. The 14-inch display is a sweet spot. On your desk and used with the keyboard, it is a sweet spot and a perfect middle ground between the 13.6-inch and 15-inch laptops, but it feels very large in hand when you hold it and use it as a tablet.
The OLED display is one of the best I have seen on a tablet, matching premium, high-quality displays with 100% DCI-P3 color gamut and PANTONE validation. The blacks look deeper, and colors are represented very accurately, making it a good choice for designers and photographers who want to edit images accurately. The touch response is also fast, but Windows is the one to blame. It makes interactions less convenient, which I will cover more in the OS section.
The display also supports a stylus. ASUS includes the ASUS Pen 3.0 out of the box. Writing and drawing on the display feels faster and more fluid. But because of the glass finish, it feels slippery while taking notes. You can apply a matte-finish screen protector for a better typing and note-taking experience on this tablet. After the iPad Pro, the ASUS ProArt PZ14 provided the best note-taking experience, even better than the Apple Pencil in some cases.
ASUS, being extra generous, added the pencil-scribble sound while taking notes. Well, thank you, ASUS, for looking at those tiny details to enhance the user experience. But it sounds so artificial.
Next, this 16:10 aspect ratio is perfect for watching content. I watched three episodes of Better Call Saul (season 4) on Netflix, and the experience was better on the ASUS ProArt PZ14 than on my iPad Pro.
With 3K resolution and 243 pixels per inch, it is also one of the sharper displays. It looks sharp even when you zoom in on minor editing details.
However, if you often read web pages, blogs, or docs on this tablet, while it looks fine when using it in laptop mode, as soon as you pick it up and use it as a tablet, you are holding a massive tablet, and 16:10 feels very wide when you put it close to your eyes, which means you need to move your head to read the text. Also, portrait mode isn’t appealing either, with that 14-inch massive screen making it hard to read and scroll. With this large form factor, using it with a single hand is almost impossible. You can try if you want.
Overall, the display is one of the ASUS ProArt PZ14’s biggest strengths. Whether you’re watching content, editing, or designing, everything looks incredible on this massive screen.
ASUS ProArt PZ14 Keyboard and Trackpad: Laptop-like typing, but better suited for a desk
ASUS also provides a keyboard out of the box. Unlike with the iPads, which you need to buy separately and are also expensive. Fortunately, the typing experience is as good as on thin-and-light laptops. However, if you’re used to mechanical keyboards or longer key travel, you might find it hard to type at first, but you can eventually get used to it.
Also, there are a few things that you need to know: the keyboard completely detaches from the tablet, which means it doesn’t have a hinge that holds the display and keyboard together. A small magnetic attachment on the bottom of the tablet connects to the keyboard.
You can just hover the tablet over the keyboard, and it attaches magnetically. However, the magnet isn’t as strong, so it can also detach easily. And since there is no strong hinge holding the keyboard and tablet together, you cannot place it on your lap and type on uneven surfaces, where the tablet takes the full weight and could tip back.
Fortunately, ASUS also included a full touchpad, and again, it’s almost like using the touchpad on a regular thin-and-light laptop. The speakers are very loud. They have rich sound. There is no headphone jack.
ASUS ProArt PZ14 Specs and Performance: Snapdragon X2 Elite delivers plenty of power
Under the hood, the ASUS ProArt PZ14 runs on the Snapdragon X2 Elite X2E-88-100 processor. My variant has 32GB of LPDDR5X RAM and a 1TB M.2 NVMe PCIe 4.0 SSD. That’s a large configuration by current standards.
Qualcomm is trying too hard to become a name for its PC processors after it conquered Android phones. The processor offers very solid performance. Tasks feel faster, and it compares with some of the best in the industry right now, including the Intel Core Ultra 7 series and Ryzen AI Max+, among others. In comparison, in Geekbench single- and multicore scores, Snapdragon X2 Elite has produced very good numbers.
You can see the benchmarks of the ASUS ProART PZ14 from third-party testers.
The tablet also offers a dedicated performance mode that provides extra power when needed. This results in smooth day-to-day performance; whether it’s opening apps, touch interactions, gaming, or uploading files, everything feels smoother on this tablet
The built-in SD Express 7.0 card reader delivers strong sequential read and write rates, including 730 MB/s sequential read speeds. So if you are a creator who copies videos and files to and from the tablet, the ASUS ProArt PZ14 won’t consume your time.
However, while the processor is solid in CPU performance, the GPU is still weaker on Snapdragon processors, and the same is true of the Snapdragon X2 Elite. It comes with an integrated Qualcomm Adreno GPU. That performs decently; however, it’s not as good as Radeon or Intel Arc GPUs.
Because of this, it might not excel at higher-end applications or even gaming. It can offer decent performance, but not top-tier.
While the GPU might not be the most powerful, the NPU performance is significantly better. The Snapdragon X2 Elite includes a Qualcomm Hexagon NPU rated up to 80 TOPS. This lets you offload a few AI tasks locally for better performance. For instance, if you are a creator, you can run AI models locally.
ASUS ProArt PZ14 also comes with a fan. Under load, the tablet tends to get a bit warmer, and the fan kicks in.
Overall performance is impressive for such a thin and light device. Daily use, such as browsing the web, watching movies and shows, and running a few high-end software applications, feels faster and handles every task without breaking a sweat.
Moreover, while compatibility with popular ARM apps on Windows has improved over the years since Qualcomm announced Snapdragon X Elite, some older programs and plug-ins still aren’t natively compatible with Windows on ARM, and some run via x86 emulation.
ASUS ProArt PZ14 Battery Life: Easily lasts an entire workday
The battery life is incredible on this tablet, and Windows on ARM has already proved it. The ASUS ProArt PZ14 comes with a 75Wh four-cell lithium-ion battery. ASUS also offers a 68W USB-C charger in the box.
Even in performance and non-performance modes, battery life stays consistent. On average, I got around 12 to 14 hours of battery life with light to medium use and about 10-11 hours with heavy use, including gaming. With light use, just using the browser, I even got two days of battery life.
ASUS ProArt PZ14 Windows 11 Experience: Full desktop software, but a poor tablet interface
Now let’s address the elephant in the room: Windows 11. I would say having Windows 11 is both the biggest strength and also the biggest weakness of this tablet. The ASUS ProArt PZ14 ships with Windows 11 or Windows 11 Pro out of the box, depending on the configuration. My unit comes with Windows 11 Home.
No matter which version you are on, Windows 11 isn’t optimized for the touch interface. In Windows 11 touch mode, it feels like a desktop and has very small buttons, menus, and toolbars.
If you primarily want to use the ASUS ProArt PZ14 as a tablet, and you’re used to iPad Pro-type interaction, you will definitely find it hard to use day-to-day. Fortunately, using the pen minimizes this. However, if you primarily use your hands, keep that in mind.
Also, this tablet has a core Windows problem. The biggest problem is the annoying Windows updates. They are still an issue even after Microsoft promised to reduce those interruptions. Unfortunately, I haven’t been able to set up the tablet from scratch because it’s a pre-owned unit, and someone else has already set it up for me, so I was saved from dealing with lengthy setup processes.
Another big limitation of Windows running on ARM is limited app support. While app support has improved significantly since I first reviewed the Snapdragon X Elite laptop, most popular applications are now natively available on Windows on ARM, but a few legacy applications still use Prism emulation, which affects performance and misses core features. However, if you mainly want to use it as a creator tablet, most creator apps are natively available on Windows, and a few games are also natively supported on Windows on ARM.
But the biggest advantage is that, since it runs on Windows, you can run full desktop-level software without any limitations. You can multitask with multiple windows. If you want better multitasking and portability at the same time, this is something you should get.
ASUS ProArt PZ14 Ports and Connectivity: USB4 and SD Express are useful, but some ports are missing
Despite its tablet form factor, ASUS has included decent port support on the ASUS ProArt PZ14. It comes with two USB 4.0 Gen 3 Type-C ports that support up to 40 Gbps, which can be used to connect external SSDs, docks, and even an external monitor.
It also includes an SD Express 7.0 card reader, which is excellent for transferring video and photos from your cameras. There’s no HDMI port, which I miss, but you can easily work around it with external peripherals. The camera quality is also good, much better than the webcam quality on other ASUS laptops I have tested. The rear camera is also decent in good lighting, which you can use to scan documents quickly. The tablet also supports Wi-Fi 7 or Bluetooth 6.0.
ASUS ProArt PZ14 Verdict: A powerful Windows tablet for creators on the go
So, that is everything that you need to know about ASUS ProArt PZ14. With its excellent display, tablet-first design, portability, battery life, and solid performance, it is a great pick for anyone who wants a powerful tablet on the go.
The 3K OLED display also makes it a great option for entertainment whenever you want to watch content or even play games. Overall, the ASUS ProArt PZ14 is a great option for a creator-first experience and for anyone who values portability and wants an all-in-one tablet that can replace a conventional laptop and a tablet at home. However, the tablet costs Rs 2,69,990 for 32GB LPDDR5X RAM. It is expensive.

- Lightweight and highly portable
- Strong Snapdragon X2 Elite performance
- Excellent battery life
- Keyboard and ASUS Pen included

- Weaker GPU performance

Election commissioners SS Sandhu and Vivek Joshi with Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar
NEW DELHI: Two of three election commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, formally objected at least 14 times in 10 months to decisions taken in the full Commission's name, according to an Indian Express report.On Wednesday, a Supreme Court-bench was split on the challenge to the law used to appoint them and asked the CJI to set up a five-judge bench.
Why it matters
The row lays bare three unsettled questions about election referee: who decides, who controls the voter database, and who picks the people at the top.Also read: What would Seshan do if faced with SIR?Here are 10 questions at the centre of the controversy.
1. What exactly are the 2 EC reported to have objected to?
The objections concern some of the most basic functions of election administration.According to the Express investigation, Sandhu and Joshi raised issues involving changes to Form 6, used by new voters seeking registration; deletion and restoration of names during SIR; appeals against decisions restoring voters; and access to and control over the electoral-roll database. Some notes also questioned communications allegedly issued in the Election Commission's name without approval of the Commission.
The EC's response is that these were inputs during decision-making, that differing opinions are natural within a multi-member body, and that final decisions ultimately had the approval of all three commissioners.
2. Can ECs disagree with one another?
Absolutely. The law explicitly expects that they sometimes will.Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023 says Commission business should, “as far as possible”, be conducted unanimously.“As far as possible” is the key phrase here.But it immediately provides for what happens when unanimity fails: if the CEC and Election Commissioners differ on an issue, the matter is decided according to the majority opinion.With three commissioners, the mathematics is straightforward: 2-1 decides the matter.The more intriguing issue in the current controversy is different: What happens if two commissioners say an action should not have been taken without the approval of the full Commission?
3. Is the CEC the boss of the other two?
The CEC unquestionably has an important institutional position, but the other two commissioners are not deputies who simply report to the chief.This question was fought over dramatically during T N Seshan's tenure. The Supreme Court upheld the creation of a multi-member Election Commission and rejected the idea that the other commissioners were merely ornamental additions. Decisions could legally be taken by majority.The 2023 law reinforces the collegial structure. It says the Commission's procedure and allocation of business may be regulated through a unanimous decision, while disagreements on substantive matters can be resolved by majority.So “Chief” does not mean the CEC has an automatic casting vote over two colleagues.In some respects, the arrangement resembles a three-judge bench more than a conventional government department headed by a secretary.
4. If disagreements are routine, why has this become such a controversy?
Because the reported disagreement is not simply over what the Commission should decide.Some of the notes reported by the Express raise an important question: Who authorised actions to be taken in the Commission's name in the first place?In April, for example, Sandhu and Joshi separately flagged communications they said had been issued without the requisite approval of the Commission, according to the investigation.The factual question is therefore not merely whether commissioners had different views, but whether the disputed actions fell within areas requiring approval by the Commission and, if so, what approval existed.The EC says its final decisions were collectively and unanimously taken.
5. Have not Election Commissioners dissented before?
Yes.Election Commissioner Ashok Lavasa disagreed with the majority in five Model Code of Conduct cases involving complaints against PM Modi and then BJP president Amit Shah. In some cases the Commission's final position was reached 2-1.But the current episode is not identical.The reported notes by Sandhu and Joshi relate heavily to administration of the electoral-roll system and the process by which actions were authorised, rather than commissioners being formally outvoted 2-1.And this time, the two commissioners raising concerns constitute two of the three members.
6. Should EC dissent be made public?
That question remains unresolved politically and institutionally.The case for confidentiality is that collegial bodies need room for frank internal discussion. Officials may become more guarded if every disagreement is immediately made public, particularly while elections are underway.The opposite argument is that disclosure can demonstrate that controversial decisions were debated rather than simply rubber-stamped.This is a practice followed by RBI and SC.At the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee, the law requires publication not only of the final resolution but also how every member voted and each member's written explanation.The Supreme Court routinely publishes majority and dissenting judgments.The Election Commission has traditionally taken a different approach. The present row has therefore revived an old question: Should an institution whose law explicitly provides for majority decisions also have a formal mechanism for publishing minority reasoning?
7. Why has electoral roll software become part of the controversy?
Because election administration is increasingly also software administration.The law places responsibility for constituency electoral rolls with statutory officials such as Electoral Registration Officers. But modern voter rolls are maintained through interconnected digital platforms.The Express investigation reports that Sandhu and Joshi questioned growing centralisation of access to the electoral database and the extent to which local statutory officials retained control. One episode cited involved 97 Goa voters who had been found eligible by electoral officials but could not immediately be restored because the software lacked the required facility at that stage, according to the report.The EC says its digital systems operate with appropriate security safeguards and that statutory election officials retain their legal powers.
8. Why SIR makes all this more consequential?
The simple answer is: Scale.The Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision has involved electoral rolls across multiple states and Union Territories. More than 13 crore names were excluded from draft rolls during the exercise across 30 states and UTs.Exclusion from a draft roll is not necessarily permanent: Voters may make claims, submit documents and pursue appeals.But depriving any electorate from casting vote for any election, howsoever local, should be treated as a serious issue in any democracy. The system needs to find a quick way to rectify it.
Delhi SIR exercise has created a peculiar scenario. More than 33 lakh voters have received notices over matters including “logical discrepancies”, prompting the Supreme Court to question whether some notices appeared to have been issued “mechanically” and ask whether additional filters were needed.
9. What’s the row about appointing election commissioners?
On September 23, Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma differed on selection mechanism of election commissioners. Justice Sharma favoured reference to a five-judge Constitution Bench; Justice Datta took a different view and emphasised that the EC must not only be independent but also appear independent. The matter is now to go before the Chief Justice for constitution of an appropriate bench.
10. So, what is the larger question raised by the EC row?
It is less about whether disagreement inside the Election Commission is healthy or unhealthy. A three-member constitutional body is designed to accommodate disagreement.The bigger issue is whether there are clear rules for what happens around that disagreement.It’s also about the sanctity of electoral rolls. No eligible voter should be deprived of their right to cast vote in any kind of polls.
Rohitashwa Ranjan is a digital journalist with The Times of India, where he decodes Indian politics as a carefully staged production with scripts, subtext and everything behind. His stories track elections, party dynamics and the things that often are buried beneath the headlines. When not parsing vote shares or alliances, he is usually reading between the lines, where the real story tends to reside.

Ai+ Smartphone has launched the Nova 2 Power 5G, the latest addition to its Nova 2 series, combining a dual-tone design with a 7,000mAh battery and 5G connectivity.
A statement issued here said that the smartphone made its debut at a fashion show in New Delhi, where it was showcased alongside contemporary athleisure designs by Just Billi by Rashmi Chhabra. For photography, the device features a 48MP AI primary camera, an 8MP ultra-wide camera and a 13MP front camera. The smartphone packs a 7,000mAh battery with 33W fast charging. It also carries an IP65 rating and supports dual 5G SIM, Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.4.
The Nova 2 Power is available in Blue Gold Fusion and Blue Fusion colour variants, with additional colours listed by the company including Ocean Green, Deep Purple and Midnight Black.
Madhav Sheth, CEO of NxtQuantum Shift Technologies, said the smartphone was designed to combine expressive design with performance and endurance.
The Nova 2 Power 5G will be available on Flipkart from September 24, with prices starting at Rs 15,999, including bank offers.

In September 2026, images circulated on social media purportedly showing a sculpture of Jesus Christ completely covered in red paint and holding an Uzi submachine gun in each hand.
"BLASPHEMY: Statue of Christ crucified holding machine guns triggers uproar from Catholics," one Facebook post (archived) read.
(Facebook page LifeSite)
Photographs of the sculpture spread across Facebook, TikTok and Reddit. Snopes readers also searched our website for information about the images.
In short, the images were authentic. They showed a real sculpture by French artist James Colomina, who confirmed to us via email that he created and installed the artwork at L'Aérosol, a network of spaces devoted to hip-hop and street art in Marseille, France, in September 2026.
What we know about the sculpture
Colomina posted photographs of the sculpture to Instagram on Sept. 10, describing the work as "Tu ne tueras point," which is French for "Thou shalt not kill." The post's description read in full:
Thou shalt not kill.
L'Aérosol, Marseille, 2026.
We invented religions, laws, and principles.
Then we invented a thousand reasons to break them.
In an email, Colomina confirmed that the photographs showed the actual physical sculpture, which he installed at L'Aérosol on Sept. 7. "The sculpture is made of resin and painted red," he said, adding that it "measures approximately 2 meters (6.5 feet) from head to toe." He also confirmed that the weapons depicted in Christ's hands were intended to be Uzis.
At the time, French-language coverage also documented the artwork. On Sept. 11, La Dépêche du Midi reported on the sculpture and published photographs credited to Colomina. Toulouse7 published similar details and also credited its images to the artist.
Colomina told us he personally took all of the photographs of the installation that he posted online or shared with news organizations, including images showing the sculpture both outside and inside L'Aérosol.
Why was the sculpture moved indoors?
Some news articles suggested the sculpture was moved indoors in response to public outrage.
Colomina told us he installed the sculpture outside L'Aérosol on the morning of Sept. 7, where it remained throughout the day. At approximately 11 p.m. that evening, organizers moved it indoors. According to Colomina, the decision was precautionary:
As the day went on, concern grew among the staff and organizers. They were convinced that this image, visible from the public space, would provoke very strong reactions. They were concerned about the consequences for the venue, but also about the safety of the staff and the people working there. As a precaution, they ultimately decided to remove the work from the exterior and move it indoors.
Colomina said that, to his knowledge, the decision wasn't made in response to a specific threat.
"The decision was primarily driven by the concerns of the staff and organizers about the reactions they believed the image would provoke," he said.
Le Parisien later reported that there were concerns the sculpture could be damaged if it remained outside and that its display could offend the religious convictions of some local residents.
Therefore, the artist's account suggests that the sculpture was not moved because of a specific threat or protest, but because organizers were worried the outdoor display could cause a strong reaction.
Meaning behind the sculpture
Colomina told us the work was based on the contradiction between the biblical commandment "Thou shalt not kill" and acts of violence committed in the name of religion:
"Thou shalt not kill" begins with a contradiction that fascinates me. The biblical commandment is clear: "Thou shalt not kill." And yet, throughout history and still today, people have killed and continue to kill in the name of their God, regardless of the religion they claim to follow.
He said depicting Christ holding two Uzis was intended to force viewers to confront that contradiction. "Christ is a symbol here, but the work is not aimed at Christianity or at any particular religion," Colomina said. Rather, the artwork addressed a broader discrepancy between the principles societies establish and their behavior:
Through the religions, laws and principles that structure our societies, the work confronts us with our contradictions. We establish rules, values and prohibitions, and then find a thousand reasons to break them.
All in all, the photographs circulating on social media were authentic. They showed Colomina's physical sculpture, which he installed at L'Aérosol in Marseille in September 2026. The artist also confirmed that he took the photographs himself and that the sculpture depicts Christ holding two Uzis.

England should stop trying to replicate Spain - Gordon
- Published
Anthony Gordon says that controlling games is not in the English "DNA" but the Three Lions could win major tournaments if they stop "trying to replicate Spain".
The Barcelona winger was speaking at St George's Park as the England squad prepare to take on world champions Spain on Saturday - their first match together since the World Cup.
England lost their semi-final 2-1 to Argentina, before beating France 6-4 in the bronze medal match.
Ending on a high meant England achieved their best finish in a World Cup since 1966.
But many have criticised the manner in which England were beaten by Argentina, after head coach Thomas Tuchel substituted goalscorer Gordon and went to a back five.
The tactical tweak invited pressure, with Enzo Fernandez equalising before Lautaro Martinez scored a stoppage-time winner.
Gordon said that he had "never felt worse", after the game and believes that the "scar" left by defeat may mean the England squad take a different approach in the next tournament.
"[The] scar doesn't have to be a negative one because it might lead us to victory in the next tournaments," Gordon said.
"We can't keep looking at other countries and trying to be like them, because we're not them - we're English and we have our own strengths which they don't have, so maybe we start playing the way we're good at."
- Signed instead of Rashford, Gordon is proving worth at Barca 
  - Published12 September
Gordon moved to Barcelona from Newcastle for £69.3m in the summer.
He says that the experience of playing in La Liga - with and against some of Spain's top stars - has made him realise just how different the nation's approach is to football.
He is not convinced English players can be taught to play more like the Spanish, with their intricate possession-based game.
"I'm speaking from a point of view where I feel like we are trying to replicate Spain," Gordon said.
"Because I'm in Spain, I know we have just as good players, but they have different qualities, so why are you trying to make those players the same as the Spanish players? Because the Spanish players lack the things that we have and vice versa."
England have lost two consecutive European Championship finals, and been beaten by France and Argentina in the past two World Cups.
Those outcomes have led to repeated questions about whether the team are good enough at controlling possession against elite nations.
Spain won the World Cup by beating Argentina and dominated with 65% of the ball in the final, restricting opponents led by Lionel Messi to just two shots in 120 minutes of play, neither of which hit the target.
Spain's particular style will test England again this weekend, and the Wembley hosts will look to find a response - but perhaps not by copying their opponents.
"It's not in the English DNA," Gordon said.
"I'm not sure it's something that can be taught because now I think, playing in Spain, I can speak with an educated view on the way they keep the ball is different.
"I even look at some of the decisions they take on the ball sometimes and think I'm not sure how you've seen that.
"It's the way they're built. I don't know whether it is something that maybe we can't ever put a name to, but they're definitely built different."
Gordon surprised to be taken off
Gordon's goal in the semi-final capped what was an impressive tournament for the 25-year-old and briefly had England supporters dreaming of World Cup glory.
The winger started five of England's games and also provided four assists.
He was taken off 17 minutes after putting the Three Lions ahead against Argentina and says that he was surprised to be substituted.
He says that after scoring he plays "off adrenaline" and "goes into an untouchable mode of confidence".
"It makes me feel on top of the world, especially in that moment on that stage. I felt really good," he said.
"But as a winger, to be honest, I come off most games. It's normal [for wingers].
"Obviously that substitution was different but in that moment probably yeah, but in general as a winger I expect it a lot of the time."
England had battled to a 3-2 win over Mexico in the Azteca Stadium, where they played with 10 men for over 35 minutes after Jarell Quansah's red card.
According to Gordon, the manner of that last-16 victory was a factor in the players' thinking when trying to get over the line against Argentina.
The winger also suggested that the team did not match the performances that they were creating in training.
If they had, Gordon says, they "would have dominated everyone".
He defended Tuchel's "more safe and more defensive" tactics, which sparked external criticism and in-camp disappointment.
"We shouldn't try and blame one man who's obviously trying his best and trying to win the cup for us all," Gordon said.
"As players, we could have done more to take the initiative to control the [Argentina] game. I think if we do that the manager doesn't make the decision [to use a back five].
"For me, we had the best team, we had the best players on the pitch in that semi-final, and in the last 20 minutes we didn't play the best football.
"That's something the manager can't really affect from the sideline, so I think as a group everyone together should take responsibility."

Meta is launching new VR hardware: a pair of glasses. The new Meta VR Glasses sit on your ears like a typical pair of glasses instead of being strapped over your head, but they still have immersive displays for watching movies, playing games, and getting work done. Imagine a pair of hefty black sunglasses with blacked-out lenses on the outside, but the components of a typical VR headset distributed between the device on your head and a computing puck in your pocket.
Meta’s next VR device isn’t a headset — it’s glasses
The new Meta VR Glasses offer immersive experiences in a shape that’s much easier to actually wear.
The idea is to give you a way to experience VR in a much lighter and more approachable form factor than Vision Pro or Meta Quest-style headsets. I got to try the VR Glasses at Meta’s campus this week, and as Meta walked me through some familiar VR demos like watching content, playing a game, and working from multiple screens, I was impressed by how much lighter the whole experience felt. Some of that was about the literal weight, as the glasses come in at just 100g, far less than the Quest 3’s 515g. But there was also something lighter in a more intangible way: the glasses form factor made the headset seem like something I could easily jump in and out of instead of being a whole cumbersome commitment with big head straps. It felt like a lightweight Vision Pro, and is perhaps a better execution of some of what Apple wanted to do with that device.
To keep things light, the VR Glasses’ display and the sensors are all you actually wear on your face. The separate puck connected with a wire contains the guts powering the headset: a Snapdragon Reality Elite processor, 128GB of storage, 12GB of RAM, and the battery, which Meta says will offer up to three hours of media playback, though you can continue using the glasses even while the puck is being charged.
The display is what Meta calls a 5K MicroOLED “Infinite Display.” It has 2412 x 2288 pixels per eye at 37 pixels per degree and supports a refresh rate of up to 120Hz. On the front of the glasses are two cameras for color passthrough, letting you see through to the world around you. The headset comes in small and large sizes to offer different options for width, though they cost the same.
You primarily use your eyes and hand gestures to control the glasses. You just look at elements onscreen to navigate, and the OS will highlight what your eyes are looking at using two pairs of eye-tracking cameras. To select something that’s highlighted, you can pinch your thumb and pointer finger together, and to scroll around, you make a fist and move your thumb around the top of your hand. It feels similar to the gestures from the Meta Ray-Ban Display, but those require a neural wristband; the VR Glasses instead use six external cameras to follow your hands.
Based on my demos, I think the VR Glasses will be best for entertainment because of the big virtual screen. Meta showed me a clip from James Cameron’s Billie Eilish concert film, which was impressive on a huge virtual display, and parts of the most recent NBA Finals, which was filmed on a format called VR180 that provided a 180-degree view of the court. I also got to watch some of Avengers: Endgame in what Meta characterized as a “VR Enhanced Cinema” experience made in partnership with Disney and Industrial Light & Magic. In the entire VR environment around the screen showing the film, there were graphics that thematically lined up with what was actually happening onscreen that also changed as the clip went on; when a huge energy beam appeared at a major moment in the film featuring Thor, I saw one shoot out at the top of the VR environment, too. Meta says that VR enhanced versions of Avengers: Infinity War and Star Wars: A New Hope will be available when the VR Glasses launch.
Gaming remains a major use case, too. Meta showed me a new mode for Beat Saber called Flux that supports playing with hands (though it will work with the Quest’s Touch Plus controllers, too). Instead of waving virtual sabers to hit blocks in time with the music, like in the original, Flux tasked me with moving my hands, which were each surrounded by balls of energy connected by pulsing electricity, to break through flying poles and smash targets. It makes sense when you play it, and the one song I played was really enjoyable. The VR Glasses will have more than 75 games at launch that will support the new hands-first experience (including a VR version of Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney – Dual Destinies launching in 2027), but they’ll also support the entire current Quest app catalog and can connect to Touch Plus controllers (and Bluetooth controllers).
Meta is also pitching this as a way to browse apps and do some work, and I can see the vision. In one demo, I used the glasses to mirror three windows from a nearby laptop. You’ll be able to connect wirelessly to computers or other devices with a USB-C connection, which could be useful if you want more screen real estate for work. My favorite demo from my whole session was actually one about typing. While using a special version of Instagram made for the VR Glasses, I was prompted to leave a comment on a picture, but I was able to type that comment and navigate the app using a virtual keyboard and trackpad that appeared after I laid my hands flat on the table. To my surprise, the virtual keyboard and trackpad were actually good. Of course, the experience wasn’t as speedy as using a physical keyboard and mouse, but in a pinch for a short message or email, I think it could be quite useful. (I should note it’s not technically new; Meta introduced this for Quest headsets earlier this year, and I haven’t tried it on those devices.)
The glasses cost $1,299.99 and will go on sale in spring 2027. That price puts the VR Glasses between Meta’s $599.99 Quest 3 and a high-end VR headset like Apple’s $3,499 Vision Pro, and I think that’s the right way to think about them. I don’t think they will transform the landscape of VR, especially when Meta itself has been divesting from VR software and largely moving on from the VR version of Horizon Worlds.
Meta is still planning to develop full VR headsets, the company’s VP of product for VR, Angela Chang, tells The Verge. But as tech companies chase the next big hardware category, however, a new form factor is starting to emerge: something that’s more capable than most smart glasses but less overbearing than a full-on VR headset. Google and Xreal are teaming up on XR glasses. Snap’s idea is the augmented reality-focused Specs glasses, and Meta is working on AR glasses too. The VR Glasses represent another fascinating idea of what a computer on your head can be.

Quick Answer
iOS 27 focuses on useful refinements, with better Liquid Glass controls, smarter Siri AI, natural-language Shortcuts, Safari web-change alerts, separate alarm volume, improved Photos tools, AirPods EQ, smarter password handling, and several everyday quality-of-life upgrades.
Apple has finally started rolling out iOS 27 to all eligible devices after testing it in beta for months. If you are reading this article, the update is already rolling out. If your iPhone supports it, you can go to Settings, General, Software Update, and update to the latest version.
iOS 27 isn’t a significant jump from what we have seen from iOS 18 to iOS 26. For those who are not aware, Apple has changed the version names to match the year. So instead of iOS 19, they moved it to iOS 26 to match the year 2026.
This year’s iOS 27 is more about refinement and fixing the issues that came along with iOS 26.
One of the biggest updates for most people, at least based on our insight, is the ability to refine the liquid glass design. Apple is now offering a separate setting to make your liquid glass look more frosted or transparent, and also allowing you to set different volumes for the alarms.
Plus, there is a new Siri and plenty of other Siri AI features, such as creating your own shortcuts using natural prompts. Let your password app fix compromised passwords, monitor website changes for free using Safari, and much more.
I have been testing iOS 27 for a few months now, testing its wide variety of features. In this guide, you will learn about the 27 best iOS 27 features that everybody should know and use for a better quality of life.
Table of Contents
Best iOS 27 Features You Should Know and Use
There are tens of new feature additions and improvements in iOS 27. However, not every new feature deserves your attention. There are a few features that really stood out for me and are genuinely useful in day-to-day life that everyone should be aware of. So here are my ten favorite picks before going to the comprehensive list of features.
Adjust Liquid Glass Design Transparency
It is evident that most people hated the new liquid glass design Apple introduced in iOS 26. Apple made the entire UI transparent overnight with a glossy effect, which made text hard to read and was resource-heavy.
Additionally, a few apps failed to adapt to this design perfectly, resulting in a bad user experience. However, Apple didn’t back off from the decision. Since the launch, Apple has continued to refine the liquid glass design to make it better and more usable.
In the latest iOS 27 update, Apple is offering a separate setting that lets you adjust the transparency of the liquid glass design. This setting is different from what we have covered in our TechPP videos, and here is how to use it.
Build Your Own Shortcuts Using Natural Prompts
Extensions and shortcuts are the two easiest ways to add missing features, whether it’s on your iPhone or in any browser. However, creating shortcuts isn’t always an easy task. It involves dealing with plenty of elements and actions, which can be hard for a casual user.
But that’s changing with iOS 27. The new Siri AI will now let you create a new shortcut based on simple, natural prompts. Now you can simply describe a shortcut using natural language, highlighting what it can do. For instance: A shortcut that automatically changes your iPhone wallpaper every morning or a shortcut that reminds you to drink water every two hours.
Since it uses AI behind the scenes, the possibilities are endless. You can describe whatever problem or feature you want to add through the shortcuts, and it will do it for you. However, the current implementation is not reliable for complex extensions. But it is a good start, and it will only get better in future versions.
I found using Claude or Codex to create iPhone shortcuts is the most reliable way, and it works much better for me than using Siri to create shortcuts, which often don’t get the desired results I wanted.
Let Your Password Apps Handle Your Compromised Passwords
When Apple first introduced the Passcodes app in iOS 18, it was super basic and missed a lot of the features found on other passcode management apps at the time. However, Apple continues to add new features, and the recent iOS 27 brings the ability to fix your compromised passwords automatically.
In simple words, if any of your passwords are compromised, your password app will automatically renew them into new passwords without you having to do it manually.
Password management apps are very good at finding your compromised passwords in data breaches. However, previously you had to manually visit every site and change the password yourself. But that’s going to change with iOS 27, where you can simply tap to auto-change the password, and it does it for you.
Monitor Any Web Changes in Real Time
This is my favorite addition to the Safari browser. Probably a feature that can kill many third-party apps. Apple has added a new Notify Me feature to the Safari web browser in iOS 27. It lets Siri AI monitor real-time changes on the website and notify you. Whether it’s an e-commerce price drop, real-time stock changes, or even a new article addition to any webpage, Safari can monitor it for you.
The best part is, you can describe what changes you want to get notified about in a natural prompt, and it does it for you. Also, there are no hard limits on how many trackers or websites you can track, and it lets you track changes every hour. Weekly, monthly, or even daily. The only requirement is that your device should support the Apple Intelligence feature.
Set Separate Volume for Your Alarms
Another feature that Apple should have introduced years ago is the ability to set custom volumes for your alarms in iOS 27. Previously, Apple used to have a single volume for all sounds, including alarms, calls, media, and notifications. In iOS 27, Apple is splitting that up, letting you set separate volume levels for alarms, media, and notifications.
One-Tap Access for Your Wi-Fi and Mobile Data Toggles
If you are someone who frequently adjusts the mobile and Wi-Fi toggles on your iPhone, iOS 27 is getting a very big, useful upgrade. Now, without needing to open the toggle or the entire panel, you can just individually turn your Wi-Fi toggle on and off directly from the toggle. It is enabled by default.
If you have customized it, you can just drag and drop the new network panel to get access to these features.
Auto-Paste Suggestions on Top of Your Keyboard
Another feature that Android users have enjoyed for years is now finally available on iPhone starting with iOS 27. Once you copy text or take a screenshot, the iOS keyboard now automatically suggests the recently copied clipboard text and images, which you can simply tap on and paste wherever you want.
Previously, it required you to long-press, select, and tap on the paste option to do that.
New Custom Equalizer for Your AirPods
Apple is rolling out a custom equalizer in the settings for AirPods. Now, iPhones with iOS 27 have a native AirPods equalizer in Settings to help you customize the audio output.
The new custom equalizer allows you to adjust lows, mids, and high frequencies separately. However, it is only available for devices running on H2 or later Pro devices, and for older devices, users need to rely on Apple’s Adaptive EQ.
Quickly View Photos Captured by You
One of the biggest downsides of iOS Photos is that the images captured from your iPhone are mixed with screenshots, memes, and other downloaded images saved from third-party apps. This makes it extremely hard for you to find the photos captured particularly from your iPhone. In iOS 27, Apple has added a new “Captured by Me” folder to the Photos app. It only shows the photos and videos taken with your iPhone camera, letting you easily find them.
Let Your Earbuds Automatically Pause When They Detect You Have Fallen Asleep
If you use AirPods, Apple has added another useful feature in iOS 27: your AirPods can automatically pause music, podcasts, or whatever you are listening to when they detect that you have fallen asleep.
Most apps these days offer sleep timers that automatically pause after a certain time. However, Apple’s implementation is more dynamic and doesn’t rely on a set time limit. Based on your movement, the AirPods automatically detect when you have fallen asleep and pause the music. This can be extra useful if you are someone like me who falls asleep, and it also eliminates the need for you to set a sleep timer every night.
The Phone App Automatically Shows Relevant Information While You Are on the Call
How many times have you searched for specific information during a call with a service agent? If your answer is often, then Apple has added a very useful feature for you.
With iOS 27, the Phone app on your iPhone now automatically shows relevant information when you are on a call in real time. These include your reservation numbers, order details, confirmation codes, and much more, which Apple can fetch from other Apple services. This eliminates the need for you to search through emails, messages, or other apps while speaking to customer support or during a business call.
Apple’s Mail App Is Now Better at Finding Information
If you use Apple Mail, it is getting a useful update. Starting with iOS 27, Apple says Mail search is upgraded to find more relevant information based on your search.
Now, instead of remembering the exact subject lines, names, or even words in your email, you can just use your natural tone and search for the exact information you want. Apple says the Mail app can now display more relevant information at the top of the search results, and it’s also smarter, as it can automatically identify the query and find the relevant information.
Now, You Can Set an Exact Expiry Time for Your Find My Sharing
If you use Apple’s Find My for location sharing, it is getting a useful update. You can select the exact time when your location sharing should stop. Previously, Apple only allowed you to share your location for an hour, until the end of the day, or until you manually turn it off.
But with iOS 27, Apple is giving you more flexibility, letting you choose a custom time. Now you can set a combination of days along with the hours to share your location. This also eliminates the need for you to manually remember to turn off location sharing if you have set it to indefinitely.
Now, You Can Turn Your Physical Cards Into Digital Passes
Apple Wallet app in iOS 27 lets you convert your physical cards into digital cards and store them in your Apple Wallet. Carrying a physical card can be a hassle, especially if you have multiple cards. It not only makes your wallet bulky, but also makes it hard to find the right one when you need it.
Moreover, there is a high chance that you can forget it, and it could get lost. Now, with the ability to convert your physical cards into digital ones, the Apple Wallet app eliminates all of these pain points. Plus, even if you want to carry a physical card, I would highly suggest converting it into a digital one, which can come in handy sometimes.
Improved AI Writing Tools Across the System
AI writing tools were the first Apple Intelligence features Apple introduced in iOS 18. However, Apple left them out and forgot to update them in iOS 26.
But in iOS 27, with the overall improvements in the AI features and getting close to what it has promised, Apple has also upgraded AI writing tools throughout the system.
Now, these writing tools are more advanced and improved. The best part of these AI writing tools is that they are integrated directly into the workflow.
So if you want to summarize, shorten, or fix spelling mistakes, you don’t need to switch apps. You can generate, rewrite, or correct text directly from your iPhone keyboard. Plus, Apple is also integrating these AI capabilities across the system, including Mail and the Notes app, letting you easily access them anywhere.
Easily Create Calendar Events Without Specific Details
Creating a calendar event requires you to fill in separate details for title, date, time, location, and other details. However, with iOS 27, Apple is making it easy for you to create or edit calendar events.
Now, without needing to fill everything manually, you can just create a calendar event using natural prompts.
For instance, you can ask Calendar to create a birthday event at 4 a.m. tomorrow, and it will do it for you. Calendar app can now understand details such as important keywords, dates (such as tomorrow at 4 PM), a person’s name, and other key details, and automatically create a calendar event. Plus, you can also edit using natural language.
Connect an iPhone Directly to Gym Equipment
If you own an iPhone and want to track your workout data, pairing it with an Apple Watch is the most sensible decision. However, it is expensive and can be overkill for users looking for basic fitness tracking features who don’t need distraction on their wrist.
However, the Apple Watch has this nifty feature where they connect to your gym equipment and receives live workout data, such as your speed, distance, pace, resistance, and the duration of your workout, which you can then measure and analyze in your Apple Health app.
If you do not own an Apple Watch or don’t want to carry it during your workout, Apple in iOS 27 has added the same GymKit functionality directly on your iPhone. So now your iPhone can directly connect to your compatible gym equipment and receive the live workout data. Plus, if you have an Acura Pro 3, you can also connect and track your real-time heart rate information.
Pause Location Sharing Without Disabling It Permanently
If you use Find My to share your location with others, iOS 27 is adding the ability to temporarily hide your location without permanently ending location sharing completely.
In previous versions, if you wanted to temporarily stop sharing your location, whether it’s because your iPhone battery is running out, or if you are planning a surprise, or if you don’t want to reveal your destination, you needed to permanently stop location sharing.
With iOS 27, you can temporarily hide your location from a person. The best part is that the person does not need to be removed, and you also do not need to remember to turn the location back on after the situation has ended.
New Improved Cleanup Tool for Your Photos
I personally hate AI photo editing features inside the Photos app. Recently, both Apple and Google have added several features that are designed to alter and convert your photos into AI-generated ones. However, one feature that I found very useful is the ability to remove unwanted people or objects from a photo directly in the Photos app without relying on third-party tools.
However, Apple’s initial version of the Clean Up Tool isn’t as great as expected. It struggled to remove unwanted distractions from an image. However, with iOS 27, Apple has significantly improved it. Now it’s on par with other clean-up tools that perfectly edit the image naturally, without leaving smudges or empty patches.
Automatically Organize Safari Tabs by Subject
With iOS 27, Apple’s Safari browser can now automatically organize tabs for you. Many other browsers have adopted this feature, but it took some time for Apple to implement it.
If you use the Safari browser and have many tabs open, you can enable the Auto-Organize feature so that it automatically organizes your tabs. This lets you easily find them or close all of them at once.
Generate Your Own Extensions for Safari
Similar to iOS Shortcuts, you can also generate your own extensions using natural prompts in Safari. If you have an Apple Intelligence-supported iPhone, you can just visit the extension tab and give it a natural prompt about what exact features the extension might have, and Apple Intelligence will create a fully working extension for you.
You can just use this extension for an individual web page, or for all the web pages in your Safari browser.
New Siri for Agentic Tasks
Apple is finally close to delivering the Siri it promised two years ago. With iOS 27, Apple is introducing the new Siri, called Siri AI, which is now better at answering your questions and also better at agentic tasks. Plus, it can now search across your Apple apps, including Mail, Messages, Photos, Notes, and all other supported apps, and get information for you.
You can create a reminder, edit a message, organize details, or complete another task. Plus, Siri can also have better context, which means it can remember the information that it gets from other apps. Although at its current stage it is not as advanced as Gemini or other intelligent or agentic AI tools, it is a good start for Apple to deliver what it promised.
It will only get better from now on. Plus, Siri is directly integrated into the system. You can activate it from any screen. Plus, it is free to use without any limitations, except for a few features that Apple might put behind a subscription paywall in the future.
New Wallpaper Extensions
If you customize your iPhone and set a new wallpaper often, this can come in handy. Apple is introducing a new wallpaper extension feature in iOS 27, which expands your wallpaper so it fits correctly based on your iPhone dimensions.
In most cases, if your iPhone wallpaper doesn’t match your iPhone screen dimensions, it can look blurry and pixelated. Plus, if you want to set it as a lock screen wallpaper, it can also affect the depth effect, making the overall wallpaper look blurry and clumsy.
With this new extension wallpaper, Apple now extends the wallpaper to perfectly fit your iPhone’s aspect ratio. The best part is it preserves the main subject and only generates the matching scenery at the image’s edges, so that the subject stays in the middle without being cut off.
Reply Inline to the Messages From Android Users
With the iOS 27 update, Apple is putting an end to another discussion of blue and green bubbles and Apple’s tactics to limit RCS messaging.
Apple iMessage now supports inline replies, where you can directly reply to a specific message sent from your Android friend. This is like a nested reply where you can long-press on any message and tap on Reply. Along with your reply, the other person’s message appears on top, making it easy for them to spot and understand.
New Siri Visual Intelligence
Siri is also now upgraded with better visual intelligence, and it is now live inside your camera app. Now you can spot objects inside your camera and ask Siri to describe them. This can be especially useful for visual intelligence tasks, such as translating the text from a photo, identifying a specific object or food, or extracting the details from a flyer.
Plus, the best part is that, since it is being done by Siri, you can also ask follow-up questions and even delegate tasks, such as adding the extracted information to your calendar or splitting and storing it in any app. Now, adjust your lock screen clock to make it look smaller.
This can be small, but useful for people who often customize their lock screen.
Apple is now letting you adjust the clock size on your iPhone lock screen. Now you can adjust the size of the lock screen clock even smaller. If you feel your clock is covering the important details of your wallpaper, or if you want it to take up less space, you can simply use the smaller clock feature to adjust its size and make it look smaller.
Organize Your Photos Better
While Apple’s Photos app search is smart enough to find the relevant image you are looking for using just natural prompts, Apple is also letting you add individual star ratings and keywords to the photos. Starting with iOS 27, you can rate the photos up to 5 stars and add keywords.
Photos app displays these details while you are browsing your media library, letting these photos stand out from the rest. This makes them easy to spot instead of manually comparing photos to find the best ones from your extensive media library.
Save Photos Directly From Videos
With iOS 27, Apple also introduced the ability to save any frame from a video. You can simply use the Save frame as a photo feature, and the video frame will be saved as a photo. You can save multiple frames as photos.
Here is how:
- Open the Photos app on your Phone
- Play any video and tap on the three-dot menu at the top
- From here, tap on the Save Video frame as a photo option
Get the Most Out of iOS 27
Those are the 27 best iOS 27 features that everyone should know and use.

GB sniff Road Worlds chance with Pogacar absent
- Published
Great Britain's impressive rider line-up for cycling's Road World Championships means the team have rarely stood a better chance of glory.
For the men, there is also the helpful factor of Slovenian superstar Tadej Pogacar being absent, after he suffered crash injuries during the Vuelta a Espana in August.
But at the same time a new generation of British cycling talent is rising, and GB riders could take the coveted winner's rainbow jersey in the men's and women's road races in Montreal this weekend.
While Pogacar crashed out of the Vuelta, the race showcased the continued emergence of 21-year-old British rider Matthew Brennan, who won five stages of the three-week endurance test for Visma Lease a Bike - a record for a Grand Tour debutant.
There are currently 49 British riders competing across the men's and women's world tours - more than ever before - and some of those will compete in this World Championship weekend.
The road race itself is much like a stage of the Tour de France, but in which riders compete in national squads, looking to out-think and out-muscle each other.
A lot of the British potential is thanks to the inspiration of British cycling's golden period, which featured great success from the likes of Team Sky, Mark Cavendish and Lizzie Deignan across the past 15 years.
Deignan won the road race in 2015, while Cavendish triumphed in 2011.
In total, British riders have won the elite road races seven times, including Tom Simpson (1965), Beryl Burton (1960 & 1967), Mandy Jones (1982) and Nicole Cooke (2008).
Amid an unpredictable performance landscape for the women, Britain's best young female riders have a chance to infiltrate the once-dominant Dutch contingent.
Tour de France Femmes winner Demi Vollering remains the sport's best overall, but Briton Zoe Backstedt's brilliant second place in Sunday's Worlds time trial was her first shot at the elite level.
She will be involved in Saturday's women's road race, and Olympic mountain bike gold medallist and Tour de France stage winner Tom Pidcock will race for the men on Sunday.
"You need a lot of faith in your team to be present at the front," Backstedt told BBC Sport. "You need to talk, hear, see and feel each other to know they are there, especially as there's no team radio.
"Obviously it's about knowing the big names to follow. If Demi or Kasia [Niewiadoma] go off the front, you know it's a dangerous move and you need to be there.
"But we've got a super strong team, and if any one of us was with them, we all could stand have a chance."
The women's road race is 180.4km long, which includes eight laps of Montreal, and the men's 273.2km race incorporates 12 circuits.
The art of the breakaway
One key way to win a road race at the Road Worlds is by breaking away from the peloton with a certain distance of the race left to run.
The risk is that one, or a handful, of cyclists find it much harder to win a race by riding into the wind than a peloton of more than 100 riders all taking turns in what can be known as the 'washing machine effect'.
But, if the legs are good and the wind is with them, riders can break away for glory.
"Sometimes you are surprised when you hit the wall, but other times you can push harder and dig deeper," Norway's Sigrid Haugset told the BBC's More Than the Score podcast.
The Uno-X Mobility rider won stage three of this year's Tour de France Femmes after a huge 113km breakaway in which she beat more decorated rivals, such as Belgium's Lotte Kopecky.
"That's the good day - when you feel unstoppable. But I like it when there is plenty of noise [on the team radio from the car]. If it's too little, you get into your head, you feel a bit alone."
Steve Cummings is sporting director at World Tour team Jayco Alula and a former GB rider and breakaway stage winner on both the 2015 and 2016 Tours de France.
Assessing the thrill of a breakaway win, he told More Than the Score: "It's like an underdog victory, and it kind of warms the heart. You have to go all-in. It becomes unpredictable and things can happen tactically and physically - say if a rider pushes too much on a climb.
"That day [in 2015] I did the climb of my life. I was empty for two days after [the 2016 win] and I was in bed for two days after [a Dauphine stage win]. It takes a lot out of you."
